title: Kitap mitap
goal: Use m-doubling and common word pairs, and follow a longer text that plays with word order, topics and emphasis.

intro.text: Repeat a word with *m* in place of its first consonant, or before its first vowel, and you get **… and the like**: *kitap mitap*, *okul mokul*. Turkish also has fixed pairs: *ıvır zıvır* (odds and ends), *eş dost* (friends and acquaintances), *er geç* (sooner or later). Both belong to everyday speech.

vocab.en: the whole family, children and all
soundly (mışıl mışıl uyumak: to sleep soundly)

exercises.en: No lessons or anything today, we're going to the park!

accept: mers

reject.why: The echo changes the first consonant to *m*: *ders mers*.
Replace the d; don't add *m* in front of it. *M* is added only before a vowel: *okul mokul*.

exercises.explain: M-doubling replaces the first consonant with *m*: *ders mers*, lessons and all that. The tone is casual, here a little impatient.

exercises.question: How do you say **school and all that** with an echo?

why.1: Nothing is dropped: the echo keeps the whole word and adds *m* in front.
why.2: Nothing is dropped: *m* goes in front of the whole word, *mokul*.

exercises.explain: A word that starts with a vowel takes *m* in front: *okul mokul*, *ekmek mekmek*.

exercises.prompt: Çantamda bir sürü ıvır zıvır var.
accept: There are lots of odds and ends in my bag.
There are a lot of [odds and ends|bits and pieces|little things] in my bag.
There are lots of bits and pieces in my bag.
There are lots of little things in my bag.
There are loads of [odds and ends|bits and pieces|little things] in my bag.
There are plenty of [odds and ends|bits and pieces|little things] in my bag.
There is a [lot|load|pile|heap] of [junk|stuff|bits and pieces|odds and ends] in my bag.
My bag is full of [odds and ends|bits and pieces|junk|stuff|little things].
I have [a lot of|lots of|loads of] [odds and ends|bits and pieces|junk|stuff|little things] in my bag.
exercises.explain: *Ivır zıvır* (odds and ends) is a fixed echo pair: *zıvır* has no meaning of its own. *Bir sürü* is **a lot of**.

exercises.prompt: Sooner or later he'll find out the truth.
accept: Er geç gerçeği öğrenecek.
er geç gerçeği öğrenir.
er geç gerçeği anlayacak.
er geç doğruyu [öğrenecek|öğrenir|anlayacak].
O er geç [gerçeği|doğruyu] [öğrenecek|öğrenir|anlayacak].
[Gerçeği|Doğruyu] er geç [öğrenecek|öğrenir|anlayacak].
Er geç o [gerçeği|doğruyu] [öğrenecek|öğrenir|anlayacak].
exercises.explain: *Er geç* (early, late) is a pair of opposites: **sooner or later**. The future or the aorist both work for a confident prediction.

exercises.question: *Masa* starts with an m. How do you say **tables and the like**?

why.1: A plain repetition means something else (one table after another), not **and the like**.
why.2: A word that starts with *m* can't be m-doubled.
why.3: A word that starts with *m* can't be m-doubled.

exercises.explain: A word that already starts with *m* can't be m-doubled; say *falan* instead: *masa falan*, *müzik falan*.

exercises.en: At the holiday the whole family went to the village.
exercises.explain: *Çoluk çocuk* is the whole family, children and all. *Eğri büğrü* is crooked, *abur cubur* junk food.

exercises.title: Babaannemin manileri
exercises.passage:
Geçen hafta sonu babaannem Fatma Hanım'ı ziyarete gittim. Babaannem iki yıl önce ta Trabzon'dan bize yakın bir eve taşındı. Çay may içtik, biraz sohbet ettik. Sonra sordum:

— Babaanne, sen gençken mani söyler miydin?

— Söylemez olur muyum! Hem de nasıl! Düğünlerde sabaha kadar mani atardık. Bizim köyde en güzel maniyi ben söylerdim, Ayşe'yse en güzel türküyü.

Sonra gözlerini kapattı ve bir mani söyledi: “Kaşların ok dedikçe, / Kirpiğin çok dedikçe…”

— Bunu sana kim öğretti?

— Bu maniyi bana annem öğretti. Ona da annesi öğretmiş. Kim yazdı, bilen yok; maniler böyledir.

Babaannemin evinde ıvır zıvır çoktur: eski plaklar, eğri büğrü bir saz, sararmış defterler… O defterlere gençliğinde duyduğu manileri yazmış. Bana gelince, ben o gece ilk kez bir mani yazmaya çalıştım. Yedi hece, dört dize, aaba: kolay mı sandınız? Saat gece yarısını geçmişti; babaannem çoktan mışıl mışıl uyuyordu.

glossary.en: Of course I did! (literally: would I not sing?)
to sing a mani (in an exchange of verses)

exercises.translation: Last weekend I went to visit my grandmother, Fatma Hanım. Two years ago my grandmother moved all the way from Trabzon to a house near us. We had tea and so on and chatted for a while. Then I asked: “Grandma, did you sing manis when you were young?” “Did I sing them! And how! At weddings we'd trade manis till morning. In our village I sang the best manis, and Ayşe the best folk songs.” Then she closed her eyes and sang a mani: “As they keep calling your brows arrows, / And keep saying your lashes are many…” “Who taught you that?” “My mother taught me this mani. Her mother had taught her. Nobody knows who wrote it; that's how manis are.” My grandmother's house is full of odds and ends: old records, a crooked saz, yellowed notebooks… In those notebooks she wrote down the manis she heard when she was young. As for me, that night I tried to write a mani for the first time. Seven syllables, four lines, aaba: did you think it was easy? It was past midnight; my grandmother had long since fallen fast asleep.

questions.q: Where did the grandmother move from?
questions.explain: *Ta Trabzon'dan*: all the way from Trabzon.
*Bu maniyi bana annem öğretti*: *annem* stands in the focus slot, right before the verb.

questions.q: What does *Söylemez olur muyum!* mean here?
questions.explain: A question that expects no as its answer: would I not sing? *Hem de nasıl!* (and how!) confirms it.

questions.q: In *en güzel maniyi ben söylerdim, Ayşe'yse en güzel türküyü*, what does *Ayşe'yse* do?
options: It sets Ayşe against the speaker as a new topic
questions.explain: The topic `-(y)sA`: as for Ayşe. The verb, *söylerdi*, is left out.

questions.q: What was the narrator doing at midnight?
questions.explain: *Bana gelince, ben o gece ilk kez bir mani yazmaya çalıştım.*

accept: Aşağı yukarı iki saat bekledik.
aşağı yukarı 2 saat bekledik.
yaklaşık [iki|2] saat bekledik.
Biz [aşağı yukarı|yaklaşık] [iki|2] saat bekledik.
(Biz) [iki|2] saat [kadar|falan] bekledik.
exercises.explain: *Aşağı yukarı* (down, up) is a pair of opposites: **roughly**. *Yaklaşık* is the neutral word; *iki saat kadar* works too.

exercises.question: Which of these lines from traditional manis puts both the subject and the object after the verb?

why.1: Here the verb, *kâr etmez*, comes last, as usual.
why.2: The verb, *olmasaydı*, is the last word.
why.3: No verb at all: a sentence without one.

exercises.explain: In *Nerden içsin kuzu su*, the subject *kuzu* and the object *su* follow *içsin*, for the rhyme with *kuzusu*. Everyday Turkish: *Kuzu nereden su içsin?*

exercises.task: Write a mani of your own: four lines of seven syllables, rhyming aaba, on any subject. You may invert the word order for the rhyme. Then say in one sentence what it is about.
models: Bahçede güller açtı / Bülbül dalına kaçtı / Gidince sen buradan / Gözümden yaşlar taştı. Bu mani, giden bir sevgili üzerine.
Bağlamamın teli var / Teline bülbül konar / Ninem türkü söylerken / Bütün köy dinler, ağlar. Bu mani, bir türkünün insanları nasıl etkilediğini anlatıyor.
checklist: Four lines of seven syllables each: count them
Lines 1, 2 and 4 rhyme; line 3 is free
The first two lines set a scene; the last two carry the message
The word order may bend for the rhyme or the metre: *Gidince sen buradan*

accept: My grandmother was already sleeping soundly.
My grandmother was already fast asleep.
My grandmother was already sound asleep.
My grandma was already [sleeping soundly|fast asleep|sound asleep].
My granny was already [sleeping soundly|fast asleep|sound asleep].
My [grandmother|grandma|granny] had long been [sleeping soundly|fast asleep|sound asleep].
My [grandmother|grandma|granny] had (long since|already) fallen [fast|sound] asleep.
[Grandma|Granny] was already [sleeping soundly|fast asleep|sound asleep].
exercises.explain: *Mışıl mışıl* is a sound pair for quiet, deep sleep. *Çoktan* with the past continuous: she had been asleep for a long time already.
